Practical AI for real life.

Practical AI / Human judgment

Useful AI starts with a life, not a tool.

I work with AI to build tools, develop writing, and make difficult ideas easier to work with. The interesting question is not how much it can generate. It is whether the result is useful, trustworthy enough for its purpose, and worth the effort it takes to use.

This section connects the technical checks with the everyday reasons for doing the work. Build a brief for one task, read the argument behind it, or follow a practical guide. The small tool below is a working starting point, not a promise of what AI can do.

A position to start with: Let AI do more. Keep the judgment. explores the difference between delegating production and handing over responsibility.

Use / Inspect / Decide

Start with work you can inspect.

A working tool, a checkable explanation, and a way to evaluate the tradeoff. Each has a different job.

Working browser tool

AI task brief builder

Turn a rough task into a prompt with a purpose, source material, a deliverable, checks, and boundaries. Free to use, with three illustrative examples and a plain-text template.

Inspect the design and try the checks. The tool assembles text; it does not run AI.

Checkable worked example

When two answers agree and both are wrong

Work through a small mean-versus-median example. Agreement between two implementations is not an independent check when they share the wrong assumption.

Evaluation guide, not a measured result

Did the tool actually help?

Compare the task before and after, including setup, checking, cleanup, and maintenance. A polished output alone does not establish that a workflow is worth keeping.

Try the tool, follow the calculation, or use the guide to assess a task of your own. About Nolan and this work.

From purpose to practice

Choose the question you have.

Have a task in mind?

Build a clearer AI task brief. Define the purpose, inputs, output, boundaries, and checks, then copy or save the result. Three examples help you start. No AI service or account is connected.

Where should AI fit?

Decide what matters before you ask AI what to do. Start with the purpose and the constraints rather than a list of features.

What could I use it for?

Technology for real life connects specific tasks: organizing notes, making a shared plan, finding a document, and turning a rough idea into something you can share.

Did it actually make things better?

Check whether the tool made life easier, including the checking, cleanup, and maintenance it adds. Then ask what you should still decide personally.

Check the work

A convincing result is not enough.
